subject: Vendr access & SSO delegation — evidence + token next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbustech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vendr Support <support@vendr.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Vendr onboarding request — NimbusTech SOC2/CAIQ upload

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. We need to get our security profile onto Vendr so Redwood can verify our SOC 2 summary and CAIQ responses. Security wants to know what the minimal delegation looks like for automated evidence ingestion — specifically: can Redwood create a short-lived service account token in our Vendr profile that your security team can use to push objects, or do you prefer pre-signed S3 uploads?

Quick context: our SOC 2 summary and a CAIQ export are ready. We can either upload via the Vendr web UI (manual) or give you a programmatic mechanism to push files into the profile. What's easiest for Redwood while still leaving an auditable trail?

I attached a short manifest for the files (manifest attached). Can you confirm the required metadata fields and retention expectations on your side?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Security Operations
NimbusTech

Attachment: vendr_upload_manifest.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbustech.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding request — NimbusTech SOC2/CAIQ upload

Hi Aisha — great to meet you over email. Short answer: either approach works, but we prefer a scoped service account for automation because it gives us better observability into upload events (token:who, time, filename) and lets us attach a retention policy on Redwood's side.

Quick outline of options and trade-offs:
- Service account (recommended): Redwood requests a Vendr token scoped to "Profile Upload" only, TTL 7 days (ephemeral). We use it to POST files to your profile and log the request IDs in our console. Pro: auditable, handles bulk uploads. Con: vendor needs to create token or approve via admin UI.
- Pre-signed S3 upload: You generate pre-signed URLs and we push directly to S3. Pro: no long-lived credentials. Con: more coordination for bucket naming + metadata schema.

Required metadata we need in the upload (minimal): filename, evidence_type (SOC2_summary | CAIQ_export), issuer_date, sha256, agreed_retention_days. We can accept the manifest you attached — thanks.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want the service-account path: please create a token with Profile Upload scope and TTL 7 days and share the token in the Vendr secure sharing panel (or send Prod-only via our shared secret channel).
2) If you prefer S3 presigned: send a test pre-signed URL we can use to confirm the metadata mapping.

Markus / Laura — tagging you to confirm we can accept a vendor-created token and to coordinate on the upload monitoring & log retention for NimbusTech.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Programs Specialist
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vendr onboarding request — NimbusTech SOC2/CAIQ upload

Soojin — thanks for the summary. For programmatic ingestion I prefer an ephemeral service account with a narrow scope. Suggestions from my side:
- Token scope: Profile:upload only (no profile admin or deletion rights)
- TTL: 7 days, renewable only by vendor admin
- Logging: require Vendr event id on successful PUT; store that in upload audit table

Rishi — can Platform Security provision the minimal upload role in Vendr or should we ask Nimbus to create the token and share it via Vendr's secure sharing flow? If we provision on our side we keep ownership of keys; if Nimbus provides it we get clearer vendor-side attestation.

If Nimbus goes the token route, insist on a one-time use link or TTL <= 7 days. If they want S3 presigned, require a test URL and sample object with expected metadata headers.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding request — NimbusTech SOC2/CAIQ upload

Markus / Soojin — I will stand up a dedicated upload principal in our Vendr tenant with the following constraints:
- Role: upload-only (PUT to /profiles/{id}/evidence), no read or delete by default
- Token expiry: 7 days
- IP allowlist: Redwood egress ranges (to be added after token issue)
- Audit: require vendr_event_id in SOAP/response and we log to our ingestion trace table.

Soojin — can you confirm the exact metadata keys we expect from the vendor (you listed filename, evidence_type, issuer_date, sha256, agreed_retention_days). If the manifest deviates we'll map fields but want to avoid re-ingests.

I'll coordinate creating the principal this afternoon and will post the provisioning ticket id here.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@nimbustech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vendr Support <support@vendr.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendr onboarding request — NimbusTech SOC2/CAIQ upload

Hi all — quick update from NimbusTech: we completed the upload to the Vendr profile this morning. Files uploaded:
- nimbustech_soc2_summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary)
- nimbustech_caiq_export.json (CAIQ export)

Vendr profile link: https://vendr.app/profile/NT-4832 (uploads are visible under "Evidence -> Recent Uploads"). I attached the SOC2 summary for your records.

A couple of asks from our side: can Redwood confirm that:
1) The upload events are visible in your ingestion logs with vendr_event_id attached?
2) Retention is set to 365 days on these objects (per our agreement)?

If Rishi needs anything from our vendor admin side (IP range or token rotation confirmation) let us know.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Security Operations
NimbusTech

Attachment: nimbustech_soc2_summary.pdf (PDF, 340KB)
